[Will you tell them what] God has revealed to you *in the Pentateuch regarding Muhammad* <note>original Latin: *de Mabume*—a common Latinized form of Muhammad</note> [so that they might dispute] with you regarding him before your Lord on the day of judgment, [alleging him] to be a *Prophet*, and you did not follow him? Is it then that as often as [a messenger] comes [to you with] that which your souls do not desire, you proudly refuse [it? For] some of them you will charge with lying: and some you will kill.

106. **W**hatever we have abrogated <note>original: *abrogaverimus* — This refers to the doctrine of *Naskh*, where later revelations might modify or replace earlier ones.</note> (*from the Quran*), or caused to be <unclear>forgotten, we bring</unclear> another better than it, or like it. Do you not know that God is powerful over all things? 107. Do you not know that God rules heaven and earth? Nor is there for you, besides God, any protector or helper. 108. Do you wish to demand from your Messenger (*that is, Muhammad*) that which was demanded of old from Moses by the Israelites? But whoever exchanges faith for infidelity (*or doubt for certainty*): he has certainly strayed from the evenness of the way. 109. Many of the People of the Book <note>original: *populo Libri* — a literal translation of the Arabic *Ahl al-Kitāb*.</note> wish that they might turn you back into infidels after your faith, because of their own excessive and malicious envy; even after the truth was made manifest to them: but forgive *them*, and turn away *from them, until God sends forth His command regarding the bringing of war upon them*: for God is powerful over all things. 110. And perform your prayer, and give alms: and whatever good you send before you, you shall find it with God: certainly God sees all things that you do.

111. And the *Scripturalists* <note>original: *Scripturales* — those who follow the written scriptures of the Bible.</note> said: No one shall enter Paradise, unless they are Jews or Christians. This is their hope: say to them, Bring your proof *concerning this matter*, if you are truthful. 112. Nay, rather *others shall enter*. ...God, however, calls to Paradise and to forgiveness <note>original: "indulgentiam"</note>, and He declares His signs to people, so that they might remember. They ask you about menstruation. Answer: *It is a harm* <note>original: "malum," here referring to physical discomfort or ritual impurity</note>; therefore, stay away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they are purified. When they have been purified, come to them as God has commanded: for God loves those who repent and He loves those who are clean. Your women are a field for you. Come, therefore, to your field however you wish: and send forth some good work for your souls <note>original: "opus conjugii," referring to intentions or prayers before intimacy</note>: and fear God: and know that you will meet Him. And announce glad tidings to the Faithful. 225. And do not make God an object of your oaths, claiming that you will act justly, and be pious, and maintain peace among men: for God is the hearer, the knower. 226. God will not punish you for what is unconsidered <note>original: "inconditum," meaning a thoughtless or accidental oath</note> in your oaths: but He will punish what your hearts have earned (that is, *what they have approved by their consent*): for God is the forgiver, the clement. 227. For those who have sworn that they will not have relations with their wives, a waiting period of four months is granted. If they return to them <note>original: "resipuerint," meaning to return to one's senses or the marriage bed</note>, *and it is released from the oath*, and they have relations with them: then God is the forgiver, the merciful. 228. But if they have decided upon a divorce <note>original: "repudium"</note>: God is the hearer, the knower. 229. And divorced women shall wait for themselves for *three* menstrual cycles: nor will it be lawful for them to hide what God has created in their wombs, *whether it be the menses or offspring*, if they believe in God and the last day. And for their husbands, it is more just that they seek to bring them back *even if the women refuse*, if they themselves wish for reconciliation *toward their husbands according to what is fitting for husbands to provide, kindly and humanely*. But it is fitting for men to have a degree of authority over them: and God is the powerful, the wise. 230. Divorce may be revoked twice: after that, it is fitting to either retain wives with recognition (that is, *humanely*) or to dismiss them with beneficence. Nor is it lawful for you, O husbands, to take back anything of what you have given them as a dowry when you divorce them, unless both spouses fear that they cannot uphold the limits (that is, *the prescriptions*) of God. If you fear that they cannot uphold the limits of God, it will not be a sin if the wife redeems herself <note>This refers to 'Khula,' where a woman may initiate divorce by returning her dowry.</note>. These are the limits of God: do not transgress them. For whoever has transgressed the limits of God, these will be the unjust. 231. If he has divorced her a third time, she shall not be lawful to him afterward until she has married another man, and he has had intercourse with her. Then, if the second husband divorces her, it will not be a sin upon the two of them (namely, *the first husband and the wife*), if they mutually return to marriage after a time, provided they believe that they can maintain (that is, *that they are able to observe*) the limits of God; He declares these to a people who have knowledge. 232. When you have divorced your wives, and they have reached their term (that is, *the end of the waiting period from the day of divorce until a new marriage*): retain them with kindness (that is, *without injury*), or dismiss them with recognition (that is, *dismiss them beneficently*). Do not retain them violently, so that you act unjustly against them, forcing them into what is unlawful, or toward separation, or toward a longer confinement. Whoever does this will indeed be unjust against his own soul. And do not take the signs of God in jest: remember the grace of God upon you, and *the fact* that He has sent down to you the Book of the *Quran*, and wisdom: God exhorts you, and fear God: and know that God is the knower of every thing. 233. When you have divorced your wives, and they have reached their term (that is, *the time for new marriage*), do not prevent them from marrying their husbands, if they have agreed among themselves with recognition (that is, *legitimately and fittingly*). This is preached to whoever among you believes in God and the last day. This is more convenient for you, and purer, regarding the suspicion that might be feared *on account of disagreement and the struggle of love between them*: and God knows, but you do not know. And mothers shall suckle their children for two complete years...

<meta>This page continues the translation and commentary of Surah II (Al-Baqarah) of the Quran, specifically moving through the "Ayat al-Infaq" (Verses of Spending). The previous page established the spiritual merits of charity; this page details the ethical conduct required for charity to be accepted by God, using vivid metaphors of gardens and stones. Due to the damaged left margin of the original manuscript, several opening words have been reconstructed based on the Latin context and the underlying Arabic verses (261–274).</meta>

# Sections in Surah II of the Quran

[Fear] God, then it shall be repaid to every soul what it has earned, [nor shall they be dealt with] unjustly. 282. <note>The Latin text labels this verse 283.</note> O you who have believed, when [you contract a debt with one another] until a named term <gloss>that is, until a certain [time]</gloss>, [write it down. But if he who [owes the debt is] foolish, or weak, or not able to dictate himself: [his guardian] shall dictate [with justice]: and call to testimony two witnesses from [your] men. [If there] are not two men, at least let there be one man and two women from [those you approve as] witnesses. * If one of them should err *through forgetfulness*; [the] other [of them] shall remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse whenever [they are called]: and do not be weary of writing down that *testimony or* debt, until the term of its payment. This [is more] just for testimony [before God], and easier, so that you do not doubt [the amount] and the term of its payment. But if it be a [business transaction conducted] between you, giving and receiving in the present without [delay], there will be no sin upon you if you do not write [it. But bring witnesses when] you sell to one another: and let no harm be done to the Scribe, [nor to the witness, lest he depart] from truth and justice. If however you do this, certainly [it will be a sin in] you. And fear God, and God will teach you: and God [is the Knower of all things]. And if you are on a journey, and do not find a Scribe, [let there be a pledge taken in] place of a written document <term>chirographi<gloss>a handwritten legal bond or contract</gloss></term>. And [God knows what you are] doing. 284. <note>The Latin text labels this verse 285.</note> To God belongs what is in the Heavens, and what is on the earth; [and whether you reveal] what is in your souls, or hide it, [God will take account of] it: and He will forgive whom He wills, and punish whom [He wills; for God is] powerful over every thing. 285. <note>The Latin text labels this verse 286.</note> The Messenger <gloss>that is, Muhammad <note>original: "Mahumetes"</note></gloss> believed [in what] was [sent down] to him from his Lord: and the Faithful also [believed] in God, and His Angels, and His books, and His Messengers. # *In the Name of God*

<margin>1.</margin> **A** L. M. <note>original: "A. L. M." These are the *Muqatta'at* or "mysterious letters" that appear at the start of several chapters in the Quran. Their exact meaning remains a subject of theological debate.</note> 2. *God: [there is no God but He, the Living, the Eternal].* 3. *[He] has caused to descend upon you [the Book in truth, confirming that which] had been handed down before it: and [He] desc[ended the Torah and the Gospel]* 4. *previously; as a guidance for men: and [He descended the Criterion <term>Criterion: referring to the 'Furqan,' the ability to distinguish truth from falsehood</term>. Truly, those who] have denied the signs of God, for them there will [be a severe punishment: for God is Mighty,] possessing the power of avenging.* 6. <note>The Latin numbering skips to verse 6 here.</note> *Truly [nothing is hidden from God, either on Earth]* *neither in Heaven: He is the one who fo[rms you in the wombs as He wills].*

### Key Vocabulary from the Text
*   **God** <note>original Latin: *Deus*</note> — The divine name.
*   **In Heaven** <note>original Latin: *in Coelo*</note> — Referring to the celestial realm.
*   **Of avenging** <note>original Latin: *ulciscendi*</note> — Referring to divine justice or retribution.
*   **Signs of God** <note>original Latin: *signa Dei*</note> — The miracles or verses that prove divine authority.
*   **Guidance for men** <note>original Latin: *directionem hominibus*</note> — The purpose of revealed scripture.

# [Excerpts] from Surah III of the Alcoran

...just as that [wound]: and these days we make to succeed [one after another among men, so that] God might know those who believed, and take [from you witnesses <gloss>that is, martyrs</gloss>]: and God does not love those who do injustice. 141. And [so that God might purge] those who believed, and destroy the unbelievers <note>original: *infideles*</note>. 142. Or did you think [you would enter] Paradise <note>original: *Paradisum*</note>, when God has not yet known those among you who fought; nor has He [yet] known those who are patiently enduring. 143. And indeed [you were desiring death] before you encountered it. But now you have seen [it with your own eyes while you were looking on], but you fled from it. 144. And Muhammad is nothing [but a messenger <note>original: *legatus* — literally "envoy" or "legate"</note>]; messengers have passed away before him: if therefore he should die, or be killed, [will you turn back] upon your heels? <gloss>that is, will you return to unbelief?</gloss> But he who [turns back] upon his heels will certainly not harm God at all: and [God will reward] those giving thanks. 145. And it is not for a soul <gloss>that is, a person</gloss> [to die except] by the permission of God, as it was written in the book [defining the span of life]. [And whoever] has desired the reward of this world, We will give him from it: [and whoever has desired the reward] of the world to come, We will give him from it: and soon [We will reward those who give] thanks. 146. And how many of the Prophets <gloss>that is, how many Prophets</gloss> [were there with whom] many thousands <note>original: *myriades*</note> of fighters fought: yet they did not lose heart [because of] what had happened to them in the path of God: and they did not become weak [nor did they submit]. And God loves those who are patiently enduring. 147. [And their word was nothing] else, except that they said: Our Lord, spare us [our sins] and our transgressions in our affairs: and make firm our feet [against] the unbelieving nations. 148. And God gave them the reward [of this world, and the] beauty of the reward of the final world: and God loves [the doers of good].

149. **O** you who have believed, if you obey those who are infidels <note>original: *infideles* — referring here to the unbelievers or those who reject the faith</note>, they will make you turn back upon your heels, and you will return lost. 150. But God is your Lord: and He is the best of helpers. 151. Soon we will cast fear into the hearts of those who are infidels, because they have associated with God that for which He sent no proof: <gloss>namely, He did not reveal nor permit men to do so</gloss> and their dwelling shall be the fire: and most wretched is the resting place of the Unjust. 152. Now indeed, God has fulfilled His promise to you, when you were destroying them by His command: until you trembled and grew faint from weariness; and discord arose among you in the matter; and you were rebellious after He had shown you that which you loved <gloss>that is, the spoils of war</gloss>: there were some of you who desired this world, and there were some of you who desired the world to come. Then He turned you to flight from them, that He might test you: and indeed He has already forgiven you: and God is full of grace toward the faithful. 154. *Remember*, when you were ascending the mountain, and you did not look back at anyone. And the Messenger <note>original: *Legatus* — referring to Muhammad</note> was calling you from behind your back. Therefore, *God* repaid you with affliction upon affliction, so that you would not grieve over what had been snatched from you <gloss>that is, concerning the spoils</gloss> nor over what had happened to you. For God was well-informed of what you were doing. 155. Then after the affliction, He sent down upon you security; namely, sleep, which covered a part of you: but another part had already made their own souls anxious, thinking of God something other than the truth—the thoughts of ignorance <note>original: *stultitiæ* — literally "folly" or "stupidity," referring to the pre-Islamic period of "Jahiliyyah"</note>, saying: "Do we have anything in this matter?" <gloss>namely, in the mission of Muhammad</gloss>. Say: The whole matter belongs to God. They were hiding in their souls what they did not manifest to you: they said: "If we had anything of this matter <gloss>that is, if we were certain of victory</gloss>, we would not have been killed here." Say: Even if you had been in your houses, surely those (for whom slaughter had been prescribed by *God* from eternity) would have gone forth to the places <unclear>cu-runt</unclear>; and so that God might test what was in your breasts; and that He might purge what was in your hearts: for God is the Knower of what is in the breasts. 156. Certainly, those of you who turned their backs on the day the two armies—the faithful and the infidels—encountered one another at Uhud <note>original: *Ohod* — the site of a famous battle in 625 CE where the early Muslims suffered a setback</note>, Satan made them slip because of some *sin* they had committed: but God has already pardoned them: for God is forgiving and mild. 157. O you who have believed, do not be like those who were infidels and said of their brothers when they traveled through the land <gloss>that is, they died while traveling for worldly business</gloss> or when they were killed while fighting: "If they had been with us, they would not have died, and they would not have been killed": so that God may make this *saying* of theirs a source of grief in their hearts. But it is God who gives life and causes death: and God is the Seer of what you do. 158. And certainly, if you are killed in the path of God, or if you die: surely forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what you gather <gloss>namely, worldly riches</gloss>. 159. And indeed, whether you die or are killed, unto God you shall be gathered. 160. By mercy from God, you were made gentle toward them, O *Muhammad*. For if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would surely have dispersed from around you. Therefore, pardon them and ask forgiveness for them: and consult them in the matter of *war*: and after you have taken a certain counsel, trust in God: for God loves those who trust *in Him*. 161. If God helps you, no one will be your victor: but if He deserts you, who is there that will help you after Him? In God let the faithful trust. 162. And it is not for a Prophet to defraud: but whoever defrauds shall come with what he defrauded on the day of resurrection: then every soul shall be fully repaid for what it earned, and they shall not be treated with injustice. 163. Is he, then, who follows the good pleasure of God like him who has drawn upon himself wrath from God, and whose dwelling shall be the fire of Gehenna <note>original: *Gehennæ* — Hell</note>? Most wretched is the arrival there. 164. These shall be degrees...

But if there are *only* women, *and these are more than two; let two-thirds of that which the deceased left behind be given to them.* But if there is *only one, let half be given to her.* And to the parents of the same deceased person, let a *sixth part be given to each of them from what he left, if he has a son.* But if *he has no son, and his parents are his heirs: then a third part shall be given to his mother.* But if *he has brothers; a sixth part shall be given to his mother, after the fulfillment of legacies he may have bequeathed, or the payment of debts he may have left behind.* Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them are *literally* closer to you in utility <note>that is, more useful to you</note>. *This* is a statute from God: for God is all-knowing and wise. 11. And to you is owed half of what your wives leave behind, unless they have offspring. But if they have offspring, then *a fourth part of what they left shall fall to you, after the fulfillment of legacies they bequeathed, or the settlement of debts.* To the wives themselves *a fourth part shall be assigned from what you leave behind, unless you have offspring.* But if you have offspring, then an eighth part of what you leave behind shall be established for them, after the fulfillment of legacies they bequeathed, or the settlement of debts.

But if you hold them in hatred, perhaps it will happen that you hold a thing in hatred in which God has placed much good for you.* But if you wish to exchange a wife in place of a wife; *with another wife; and you have already given one of them a talent <note>a very large sum of money or gold</note>, do not take anything from it. Shall you take it through injustice and manifest iniquity?* 19. 77. **W**herever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty towers: but if some good happens to them <note>original: *id est Judæis* — "that is, the Jews"</note>, they say: This is from God. What then is the matter with these men, that they are so close [to the point] of not understanding the discourse; <note>that is, anything of what is said to them</note>. 78. That which happens to you of good is from God: but that which happens to you of evil is from yourself. And we sent you to men as a Messenger <note>original: *Legatum*</note>: and God is a sufficient witness *of this thing*. 79. He who obeys the Messenger, has then indeed obeyed God: but he who turns away, we have not sent you as a guardian over them. 80. And they say: Obedience. But when they have gone out from your sight, a part of them revolves in their mind something other than what they said: but God writes down what they revolve in their minds. Depart therefore from them, and trust in God, for God is a sufficient advocate <note>original: *procurator*, meaning a trustee or one who manages affairs on behalf of another</note>. 81. Do they not attentively consider the Quran? For if it were from another than God, they would surely find many contradictions in it. 82. <summary>This passage emphasizes that all outcomes, both good and bad, ultimately stem from God, while also establishing Muhammad's role as a Messenger whose authority is synonymous with God's. In the Arabic text of the Quran, the word is 'yalhath', which specifically describes a dog panting with its tongue out, whether it is chased or left alone—a metaphor for a person who is never satisfied or settled in faith.</note> This is the likeness of the men who devise lies against our signs.

25. <note>In modern numbering, this corresponds to verse 24.</note> Truly, the likeness of the **worldly life** is like water which we have sent down from Heaven, and the vegetation of the earth mixes with it—from which humans and cattle eat—until the earth has taken on its beauty and been adorned *with herbs and flowers*. <note>The "people of the reminder" (familiam commonitionis) refers to the Jews and Christians, whom the Quran suggests the Meccans should consult to verify that previous messengers were indeed mortal men.</note>

<term>Alcoranus</term> — The Quran, the central religious text of Islam.
<term>Mahumetus</term> — Muhammad, the prophet of Islam.
<term>Meccanis</term> — The inhabitants of Mecca, the city where Muhammad began his mission.
<term>Prophetæ</term> — Prophets, individuals believed to be inspired by God to deliver a message.
<term>Pentateuchus</term> — The Pentateuch or Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.
<term>Evangelium</term> — The Gospel, the record of Jesus's life and teaching.
<term>commonitio</term> — A reminder or warning, often used in this text to refer to divine scripture.
<term>praevaricatores</term> — Transgressors or those who act wickedly by overstepping divine laws.

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful
<note>original: "In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis" — This is the Basmala, the standard opening invocation for almost every chapter (Sura) of the Quran.</note>

1. This <term>Sura: a chapter or section of the Quran</term> we have sent down from Heaven; and we have ordained it <gloss>that is, we have placed sanctions and decrees within it</gloss> and we have sent down in it manifest signs, so that you might be reminded.

2. The female adulterer and the male adulterer <note>original: "Scortatricem, & scortatorem" — the Latin translator uses terms often associated with prostitution to describe those committing illicit sexual intercourse (*zina*)</note>, strike each of them with a hundred lashes, and let not compassion for them take hold of you in the judgment of God, if you believe in God and the Last Day; and let some of the believers be witnesses to their punishment.

3. The male adulterer shall not marry except a female adulterer or a female associator <gloss>that is, an idolater</gloss>. And a female adulterer shall not be taken in marriage except by a male adulterer or an associator <note>The term "associator" (Latin: *associator/associatrix*) refers to a polytheist, specifically one who "associates" other deities or partners with the one God.</note>.

But they have no certain knowledge of this; they do nothing but guess. **25.** And when our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is to say: "Bring back our fathers *from the dead*, if you are telling the truth." **26.** Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die; then He will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, of which there is no doubt." But most people do not understand. **27.** To God belongs the sovereignty of the Heavens and the Earth. And on the Day when the Hour *of Judgment* arrives, on that Day the followers of falsehood will be lost. **28.** And you shall see every nation kneeling; every nation shall be called to its record: "Today you shall be repaid for what you have done." **29.** This, our Book, speaks against you with truth; for We have caused to be recorded everything that you did. **30.** As for those who believed and performed good works, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the manifest triumph. **31.** But as for those who disbelieved, *it will be said*: "Were my verses not recited to you? Yet you were arrogant and became a criminal people." **32.** And when it was said, "Truly the promise of God is true, and there is no doubt concerning the Hour," you replied, "We do not know what the Hour is; we think it is but a conjecture, and we are not convinced." **33.** Then the evil of their deeds will appear to them, and that which they mocked will encompass them. **34.** And it will be said: "Today We forget you, just as you forgot the meeting of this, your Day. Your dwelling is the Fire, and you have no helpers." **35.** This is because you took the signs of God as a joke, and the life of the world deceived you. Therefore, on this Day they shall not be taken out of it, nor shall they be allowed to make amends. **36.** Praise, therefore, be to God, the Lord of the Heavens, and the Lord of the Earth, the Lord <margin>of the Worlds.</margin> of the Ages. <note>original: "Domino Sæculorum". The translator notes in the margin that "Mundorum" (of the Worlds) is an alternative reading for the Arabic *al-ʿālamīn*.</note> **37.** And to Him belongs the majesty in the Heavens, and the Earth: and He *is* the All-Powerful, the Wise.

Upon them *shall be* the circle of evil <gloss>that is, a persevering punishment</gloss>, and God is angry with them, and has cursed them, and has prepared <term>Gehenna</term> <note>original: "Gehennam"; the Hebrew-derived term for Hell.</note> for them: and *this* is an evil destination <gloss>that is, unhappy are those who go into it</gloss>. 7. And to God belong the armies of the Heavens and the Earth: and God is All-Powerful and Wise. 8. Certainly, we have sent you as a witness against your people on the day of *Judgment*: and as an announcer of *Paradise*, and a threatener of *Gehenna*. 9. So that you may believe in God and His Messenger; and that you may bring help to him, and honor him, and praise him morning and evening. 10. Certainly, those who swear allegiance to you, truly swear allegiance to God: the hand of God *shall be* over their hands. He who violates the oath shall surely be a perjurer against his own soul. But he who fulfills that which he covenanted with God, *God* will soon give him a great reward. 11. The stay-behinds among the Arabs will say to you <gloss>that is, those who, remaining at home, refused to set out for battle</gloss>: "Our possessions and our families were an impediment to us, lest we should go out with you to war: therefore pray for indulgence for us." They say with their tongues that which is not in their hearts. Respond: Who then shall obtain anything for you from God, if He willed to harm you, or willed to benefit you? Yet God is fully informed of what you do. 12. Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the Faithful would never return to their families: and this was made fair in your hearts: but you thought an evil thought <gloss>that is, a false one</gloss> and you were a lost people. 13. And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, certainly we have prepared a blazing fire for the infidels. 14. And to God *belongs* the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth: He pardons whom He wills, and punishes whom He wills: and God is Forgiving and Merciful. 15. The stay-behinds will say <gloss>that is, those who remained at home and did not set out for battle</gloss> when you proceed to the spoils to take them: "Let us follow you." They wish to change the word of God <gloss>that is, the laws prescribed by God concerning the spoils of enemies</gloss>. Say *to them*: "You shall by no means follow us: so God said before." They will respond: "But you envy us." But they understand nothing *concerning Religion*, except for a few. 16. Say to the stay-behinds among the Arabs: "You shall be called to fight against a people endowed with strong military valor: you shall fight against them, or they shall become Muslims" <gloss>that is, until they embrace the Muhammadan Sect</gloss>. If you obey, God will give you a beautiful reward. But if you turn away, just as you turned away before: He will punish you with an excruciating punishment. 17. There shall be no sin upon the blind, nor sin upon the lame, nor sin upon the sick *if they do not set out for war*. But he who obeys God and His Messenger: He will lead him into gardens where rivers flow beneath them. But he who turns away: He will punish him with a painful punishment. 18. Already indeed, God was well-pleased with the Faithful when they swore allegiance to you under the tree; and He knew what was in their hearts: therefore He sent down a secure peace upon them, and rewarded them with a victory near at hand in <term>Khaibar</term> <note>original: "Chaiber"; an oasis north of Medina conquered by Muhammad's forces in 628 CE.</note>. 19. And with many spoils which they took: and God is All-Powerful and Wise. 20. God promised you many spoils which you would take: but He hastened these *of Khaibar* for you (and He withheld the hands of men from you) so that they might be a sign of Divine aid to the Faithful: and that He might guide you into the right way. 21. And other *spoils* you have not yet been able to take: God has already surrounded them <gloss>that is, He holds them ready for you</gloss> and God is Powerful over every thing. 22. If those who were infidels in <term>Hudaybiyyah</term> <note>original: "Hadibia"; referring to the location of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.</note> had fought against you, they would surely have turned their backs: then they would have found neither patron nor defender. 23. *This is* the decree of God which already preceded before: and you will never find a change in the decree of God. 24. And it is He who withheld their hands from you, and your hands from them in the belly of Mecca <gloss>that is, in Hudaybiyyah</gloss> after He had made you triumph over them. And God is watching what you do.

### Refutations of Sura XLVIII of the Quran

25. These *are* they who were unbelievers, and prohibited you from the <term>Place of Prayer at Mecca</term> <note>original: "Oratorio Meccæ"; referring to the Sacred Mosque or Masjid al-Haram.</note>: and they hindered the offering <note>original: "munus"; referring to the sacrificial animals intended for the pilgrimage at Mecca</note> which was prevented, so that it could not reach its place. If there had not been believing men and believing women, whom you did not know—*since they were mingled with the unbelievers*—so that you might not trample them <gloss>that is, so that you would not kill them</gloss> and consequently a sin would fall upon you because of them <gloss>that is, from their slaughter</gloss> without your knowledge: He certainly would have granted you victory. But then He wished to grant it for this cause, that God might lead whom He willed into His mercy. If the Believers had been distinct from the unbelievers: we certainly would have punished those who were unbelievers among them with a painful punishment.

26. When those who were unbelievers had placed in their hearts indignation, the indignation of <term>Ignorance</term> <note>original: "Ignorantiæ"; referring to the *Jahiliyyah*, the pre-Islamic period of "ignorance" or paganism in Arabia.</note> <gloss>that is, the characteristic of the Pagans</gloss>, God sent down His peace upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He impressed upon them the word of piety <gloss>that is, faith in the unity of God, or that formula: There is no God, but God</gloss>; and they were more worthy of that same word, and more deserving of it, than the unbelievers. And God is Knowing in all things.

27. Indeed, God has confirmed for His Messenger the vision with truth, which He spoke to him *through a dream*: You shall most certainly enter the Place of Prayer at Mecca, if God wills, secure with your heads shaved and your hair cut; you shall not fear. Furthermore, God knew that which you did not know: and He decreed, besides this, a near victory for you over the <term>people of Khaybar</term> <note>original: "Choaiberensibus"; referring to the inhabitants of the Khaybar oasis, whose defeat followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.</note>.

28. He it is who sent His messenger with guidance and the true religion, so that He might exalt it over every religion: and God is sufficient as a witness <gloss>that is, God suffices as a witness of this matter</gloss>.

29. Muhammad is the messenger of God: and those who are with him are fierce against the unbelievers; merciful among themselves. You will see them bowing themselves, adoring, *so that* they may seek abundance from God and His good pleasure. Their signs are in their faces from the traces of adoration <gloss>because, namely, they touch their faces to the ground while they pray</gloss>. This is their likeness <gloss>that is, their description</gloss> in the <term>Pentateuch</term> <note>original: "Pentateucho"; the first five books of the Bible, or the Torah.</note>. And their likeness in the <term>Gospel</term> <note>original: "Euangelio"</note> is like a seed which has produced its stalk: then it strengthened it: then it was made thicker, and it was balanced upon its legs <gloss>that is, it rose up on its own stalk</gloss>, bringing delight to the farmer. *God willed for the followers of Muhammad to be such*, so that the Unbelievers might be moved to anger through them. God has promised those among them who have believed and performed righteous works, forgiveness and a great reward.

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful <note>original: "In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis"</note>.

1. O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward in speaking or acting before God and His messenger <gloss>that is, wait for their sign and permission</gloss> and fear God; for God is hearing, Knowing. 2. O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet when you speak with him; nor be too loud with him in speaking <gloss>that is, do not speak too freely with him</gloss> as you are loud with one another <gloss>that is, as you act freely toward each other in speaking</gloss>, lest your deeds become useless while you do not perceive it. 3. Truly, those who lower their voices in the presence of the messenger of God are those whose hearts God has tested for piety. For them there will be forgiveness and a great reward. 4. Furthermore, those who call out to you from behind the private chambers: most of them do not understand what reverence is owed to you. 5. If they had waited patiently until you came out to them, it would certainly have been better for them; and God is Forgiving, Merciful.

6. O you who have believed, if some <term>sycophant</term> <note>original: "Sycophanta"; here referring to a person bringing malicious rumors or false news.</note> comes to you with a report <gloss>that is, to tell you something evil about another</gloss>, distinguish correctly whether he is truthful or a liar, lest you harm someone through ignorance and afterward become repentant for what you have done. 7. And know that the messenger of God is among you. If he were to follow your wishes in many matters, you would certainly fall into sin, because you would be the cause of him erring in many things through no fault of his own. But God has instilled in you a love of faith and has adorned it in your hearts; and He has made infidelity, wickedness, and disobedience hateful to you. These are the ones following the right path. 8. Through kindness from God and grace: and God is Knowing, Wise. 9. If two factions of the believers should quarrel among themselves, establish peace between them both. If one of them should rise up unjustly against the other, fight against the one which has acted violently until it returns to the command of God. If it returns, take care for peace between both with equity; and conduct yourselves justly in this: for God loves those who act justly. 10. Surely the Believers are brothers; therefore take care for peace between your brothers and fear God, so that you may obtain mercy. 11. O you who have believed: let not some mock others. It may well be that those who are mocked are better than those who mock them. Neither let women mock other women; perhaps it will happen that those they mock are better than themselves. Do not defame one another, nor call each other by vile or shameful nicknames. It is a most wicked name to be called "wicked" after having accepted the faith <gloss>that is, that someone, after receiving the faith, should be commonly held and called "wicked"</gloss>. Those who do not repent of this sin, they will be the unjust. 12. O you who have believed, beware much of suspicion <gloss>that is, of thinking ill of others</gloss>; for indeed, some suspicions—

# Refutations of Sura 51 of the Quran

<margin>
The Twenty-Seventh Part
</margin>

*...they announced to him Isaac, who was endowed with great knowledge* <note>original: "miserunt ei Isaac..." Though the Latin uses "sent," the context in the Quran refers to the angels bringing news of Isaac's birth.</note>). 29. But his wife approached with a cry, and she struck her face with her palms and said: "I am a barren old woman." 30. The *Angels* said to her: "Thus said your Lord: truly He is the Wise, the Knowing." 31. *Abraham* said to them: "What, then, is your business, O Messengers?" 32. They responded: "We have indeed been sent to a wicked people <gloss>that is, to the people of Sodom</gloss>. 33. That we may cast upon them stones of clay <gloss>that is, bricks</gloss>. 34. Marked by your Lord for the transgressors <gloss>that is, imprinted with the names of those upon whom they are to be cast</gloss>." 35. Therefore, We brought out those who were in that city from among the believers. 36. And We did not find in it except one house of Muslims <note>original: "Moslemis." The 17th-century translator uses the Latinized term for those submitting to God's will.</note>. 37. And We overturned it, and We left in it a sign of its ruin for those who fear the painful punishment. 38. In Moses also there was a sign of Our power, when We sent him to Pharaoh with manifest authority. 39. But he turned away with his army and said: "This is a sorcerer, or one possessed by demons." 40. Therefore We took him and his army and We cast them into the sea, and he was the one to blame. 41. And in the people of Ad there was also a sign, when We sent against them a sterile wind. 42. It did not touch any thing upon which it came without rendering it like something rotten and crushed. 43. There is no secret conversation of three, but that he is their fourth: nor of five, but that he is their sixth: nor fewer than this number, nor more, but that he is with them, wherever they may be. Then he will relate to them that which they have done on the day of Resurrection: for God is Knowing of every thing. 8. Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret conversation: then they return to that which they were forbidden, and they speak secretly among themselves of iniquity, and hostility, and disobedience toward the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that manner of greeting by which God never greeted you <note>This refers to enemies of the Prophet who used a wordplay in Arabic, saying "as-samu 'alayka" (death be upon you) instead of "as-salamu 'alayka" (peace be upon you).</note>: and they say among themselves in jest: Will not God punish us for what we say? Their sufficiency <note>original: "idest pœna, quæ illis sufficiat"; that is, the punishment which will suffice for them</note> will be Gehenna <note>Gehenna is a term used for Hellfire</note>; they shall go down to be burned in it: and wretched will be the journey to it.

<margin>* they believed.</margin>
9. O, you who have believed <gloss>a</gloss>, when you converse secretly, do not converse of iniquity, and hostility, and disobedience toward the Messenger: but converse of righteousness and piety: and fear God, to whom you shall be gathered on the day of Judgment. 10. Indeed, secret conversation about iniquitous things is from Satan, so that he may grieve those who have believed: but there will not be *any* harm to them in any thing, except by the permission of God: therefore let the Faithful rely upon God.

<margin>b they believed.</margin>
11. O, you who have believed <gloss>b</gloss>, when it is said to you: Make room in your assemblies <note>original: "idest recedite hinc inde, dantes locum Mahumeto, ut sedeat"; that is, move back here and there, giving a place for Muhammad to sit</note> make room: God will grant ample space to you. And when it is said to you: Arise: arise. God will exalt those who have believed among you, and those to whom knowledge has been given, by degrees of honor in Paradise: and God is fully informed of what you do. 12. O, you who have believed, when you are about to speak to the Messenger, offer an alms before your conversation: this will be better for you, and purer <note>original: "idest aptius ad purganda peccata vestra"; that is, more fit to purge your sins</note>. But if you do not find anything to offer: indeed God *will be* to you indulgent and merciful. 13. Do you fear that you should offer alms before your conversation, for fear of poverty? But if you do not do this, and God has forgiven you: at least observe prayer, and pay the fixed tax <term>zakat; the obligatory charity in Islam</term>, and obey God and his Messenger: and God is mindful of what you do. 14. Have you not looked at those who have taken as allies men against whom God is angry? <note>original: "idest Judæos"; that is, the Jews</note> they are not of you, nor of them: and they swear upon a lie, and they know it. 15. God has prepared for them a vehement punishment: for indeed, worst is that which they do. 16. They took their oaths as a covering <note>original: "idest ad tuendos se ipsos, & facultates suas"; that is, to protect themselves and their property</note> and therefore they turned the Faithful away from the way of God: wherefore there will be for them an ignominious punishment. 17. Their riches will not profit them, nor their children anything before God. These shall be the inhabitants of the Fire, they shall remain in it forever. 18. On a certain day God will raise them all: then they will swear to him that they are Faithful, just as they swear to you: and they will think that they stand upon something <note>original: "idest sibi hoc ad aliquid profuturum"; that is, that this will profit them in some way</note>. Are they not truly the liars? 19. Satan has prevailed over them, and has made them forget the remembrance of God. These are the followers of Satan. Are not, moreover, the followers of Satan the ones to be destroyed? 20. Certainly, those who oppose God and his Messenger: these shall be among the most vile. 21. God has written: Certainly I shall conquer, I and my Messengers: for indeed God is strong, All-powerful. 22. You will not find people who believe in God and the last day, that they love him who opposes God and his Messenger, even if they be their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their kinsmen. In the hearts of these God has written faith, and has strengthened them with a Spirit from himself <note>original: "idest suo"; that is, his own</note> and he will lead them into gardens; rivers shall flow from beneath them, to remain in them forever. God is well-pleased with them, and they are well-pleased with him. These are the followers of God; are not, moreover, the followers of God the ones to achieve happiness?

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

1. Whatever is in the Heavens and whatever is on the earth praises God; and He is the All-Powerful, the Wise. 2. It is He who drove out those who were unbelievers among the People of the Book <note>original: "familia Libri"</note> (*namely the Nadirite Jews*) from their homes at their first gathering <note>Referring to their first exile</note> into *Syria*. You did not think that they would go out from *Arabia*: and they themselves thought that their fortresses would defend them against God. But God came upon them from where they did not expect; and He cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their own houses with their own hands, and with the hands of the Faithful <note>The early Muslims</note> attacking them. Therefore, take an example *from this*, O you who are endowed with sight. 3. And, unless God had ordained for them exile (*that is, unless He had decreed they were to be driven out from Arabia into Syria*), He would certainly have punished them in this World; and for them in the world to come there shall be the torment of Fire. 4. This is because they created a schism <note>original: "schisma"; referring to their opposition or breaking away</note> against God and His Messenger <note>original: "Legatum"</note>. But whoever creates a schism against God, surely God will be severe toward him in punishment. 5. That which you cut down of the palm trees, or left them standing upon their trunks, was furthermore by the will of God, and so that He might bring shame upon the transgressing *Jews who possessed them*. 6. And that which God granted as spoil to His Messenger from them, you did not urge any horses or camels against it (*that is, you did not acquire it by means of horses or camels* <note>In Islamic law, property taken without a formal battle involving cavalry is called 'fay' and is distributed differently than 'ghanimah' or battle-spoils.</note>), but God makes His Messengers prevail over whom He wills; for God is Powerful over every thing. 7. That which God granted as spoil to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God, and to the Messenger, and to his kinsmen, and to the orphans, and to the poor, and to the wayfarer (*that is, one detained or hindered on his journey*), so that it might not be a perpetual circulation of wealth <note>original: "circulum perpetuum felicitatis"</note> among the rich from among you. But what the Messenger gives you, furthermore, take it. And what he denies you, refrain from desiring it. And fear God;

...because God *is* severe in punishment. 8. *It is* also due to the poor emigrants from *Mecca to Medina*, who were driven out from their homes and their possessions, and seek abundance from God and *His* good pleasure, and assist God and His Messenger <note>original: "Legatum"</note>. And when he had become an unbeliever, he said *to him*: "Certainly I *am* free from you <gloss>that is, from your sin</gloss>," <margin>of the Worlds.</margin> because I fear God, the Lord of *the* Worlds. 17. The inhabitants of Paradise, they will be the happy ones.

To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the Heavens and the Earth praises Him; and He is the Almighty, the Wise.

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

1. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Him: and He is the Almighty, the Wise. 2. O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do <gloss>that is, why do you say you will fight, and then you flee in battle?</gloss>? 3. It is deeply hateful <gloss>that is, most hateful</gloss> in the sight of God that you say that which you do not do. 4. Truly God loves those who fight in His way in a rank, as if they were a firmly set building. 5. And when Moses said to his people: "O my people, why do you harm me? And you already know that I am certainly the Messenger of God to you." But after they turned away *from the truth*, God caused their hearts to turn away *from guidance*; for God does not guide transgressing people. 6. And when Jesus the son of Mary said: "O children of Israel, truly I *am* the Messenger of God to you, confirming that which *was delivered* before me in the Torah <note>original: "Pentateucho," referring to the first five books of the Old Testament</note>: and announcing a Messenger *who will come after me*: his name *is* Ahmad <note>The name "Ahmad" shares the same linguistic root as "Muhammad" (H-M-D, meaning "praised") and is interpreted by Islamic scholars as a prophecy of Muhammad's coming</note>." But after *this one* came to them with clear proofs, they said: "This is manifest sorcery." 7. And who is more unjust than he who fabricates a lie against God, while he himself is called *to the Religion of Islam*? And God does not guide unjust people. 8. They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths: but God *is* to perfect His light, even if the unbelievers refuse it. 9. It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the Religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over every religion *contrary to it*, even if the Associators <note>original: "Associantes," a term used to describe those who associate partners with God, typically referring to polytheists or, in some polemic contexts, Christians due to the Trinity</note> refuse it. 10. This will be better for you, if you knew. 12. He will forgive you your sins, and will bring you into gardens beneath which rivers flow; and goodly dwellings in the gardens of Eden. This will be the great success. 13. And He will give you other things which you desire: help from God, and a near victory. And give good tidings to the Faithful. 14. O you who have believed, be helpers of God, just as Jesus the son of Mary said to the Disciples <note>original: "Apostolis," here referring to the twelve apostles of Jesus</note>: "Who will be my helpers toward God <gloss>that is, for the propagation of the Religion of God</gloss>?" The Disciples answered: "We will be the helpers of God." So a party from the children of Israel believed, and a party was unbelieving. And We strengthened those who believed against their enemy <gloss>that is, against the unbelievers</gloss>, whereby they became the victors in war against them.

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. <note>original: "In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis." This is the Basmala, the opening invocation used in almost every chapter of the Quran.</note>

<margin>Refutations of the Quran</margin>
1. When the Impious <note>original: "Impii". In the context of this Surah, this refers to the "Hypocrites" (Munafiqun)—those who outwardly professed Islam while inwardly rejecting it.</note> come to you, they say: "We testify that you are surely the Messenger of God." <note>original: "Legatum Dei"</note> And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger; but God testifies that the impious are certainly liars. 2. They have taken their oaths as a covering <gloss>that is, to protect themselves and their property</gloss> and have turned others away from the path of God. Surely, that which they have done is evil. 3. # In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

1. Read in the name of your Lord, who created: 2. He created man from a clot of blood. <note>original: *ex sanguine coagulato*. This describes the human tendency to overstep bounds or act with insolence.</note> 7. Because he sees that he has abounded in riches. 8. Surely to your Lord *shall be* the return. 9. What do you think? He who forbids 10. ### Key Terms

<term>People of the Book</term> (Latin: *Scripturalibus*): A term used to describe religious groups—specifically Jews and Christians—who received previous revelations from God.

<term>Polytheists</term> (Latin: *Associantibus*): Those who practice *shirk*, or the act of attributing partners to the one God.

<term>Clear Evidence</term> (Latin: *Evidentia*): The title of the Surah (*Al-Bayyinah*), referring to the manifest truth brought by the Prophet and the Quran.

<term>True Believers</term> (Latin: *Orthodoxi*): Those who maintain a straight and upright faith in one God.

<term>Sacred Tax</term> (Latin: *Sacrum Censum*): The practice of *Zakat*, one of the five pillars of Islam, involving the redistribution of wealth to the needy.

## In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the Basmala, the standard opening invocation for almost every chapter of the Quran.</note>

2. And what will make you understand what the Striker is?

3. On the day when men shall be as scattered locusts. <note>original: *locustæ sparsim diffusæ*. Other translations often use "moths," but Marracci uses the Latin for locusts to emphasize the swarming, chaotic movement of humanity upon resurrection.</note>

4. And the mountains shall be as dyed wool, carded apart. <note>original: *lana diversicolor discriminata*. This imagery suggests the solid mountains becoming weightless and shredded like tufts of colored wool.</note>

5. Furthermore, he whose balances shall be heavy *with good works*; he shall be in a life pleasing to himself. <note>original: *bilances*. This refers to the scales of divine justice used to weigh a person's deeds.</note>

6. But truly, he whose balances shall be light: his mother (*that is, his dwelling*) shall be the Pit. <note>original: *Barathrum*. Marracci translates the Arabic *hawiyah* as "Barathrum" (an abyss or bottomless pit). The "mother" metaphor suggests that the Pit will embrace the sinner as a mother embraces a child, but with fire.</note>

7. And what truly will make you understand what the Pit is?

8. It is a most burning fire.

# In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the Basmala, the invocation that opens nearly every chapter of the Quran, emphasizing God's attributes of mercy.</note>

1. The rivalry of multiplying worldly goods has distracted you. <note>original: *contentio multiplicandi*. This refers to the human obsession with amassing wealth, status, and children at the expense of spiritual duties.</note>

2. Until you visit the graves. <note>original: *sepulchra*. This suggests that this worldly distraction only ends when a person faces death and is buried.</note>

3. Alas! Soon you shall know. <note>original: *Vah!*. A Latin interjection used here to express a stern warning or a cry of grief, translating the Arabic *kalla*.</note>

4. Again, alas! Soon you shall know.

5. Alas! If you only knew with the knowledge of certainty. <note>original: *scientia certitudinis*. This refers to "Ilm al-Yaqin," or an intellectual and spiritual conviction that should have guided their actions.</note>

6. Surely you are about to see Hell. <note>original: *Infernum*. The Latin term used for the Arabic *al-jahim*, the blazing fire of the afterlife.</note>

7. Again *I say*: Surely you are about to see it with the eye of certainty (*that is, clearly and manifestly*). <note>original: *oculo certitudinis*. This refers to "Ayn al-Yaqin," the transition from knowing about something to seeing it with one's own eyes.</note>

8. Then, on that day, you shall surely be called to account for your pleasures. <note>original: *de deliciis*. This refers to the worldly comforts, health, and wealth that people enjoyed without giving thanks or using them for good.</note>

In Islamic tradition, it specifically refers to a river or fountain in Paradise granted to the Prophet. The Latin translator Marracci retains the phonetic Arabic name here.</note>. 2. Pray, therefore, to your Lord, and sacrifice <note>original: *jugula*. This literally means "to cut the throat," referring to the ritual slaughter of an animal (such as a camel or sheep) as an act of worship and gratitude to God.</note>. 3. Moreover, he who hates you, *he himself shall be cut off* <note>original: *ipse erit excisus*. This was a response to critics who called the Prophet "abtar" (cut off/without posterity) because he had no surviving male heirs. The verse flips the insult, stating that it is the enemy whose lineage and memory will be severed from God's blessing.</note>.

<summary>This page contains the translation of Surah Al-Kawthar, the 108th chapter of the Qur'an, which promises the Prophet Muhammad "Abundance" and commands prayer and sacrifice.</summary>
<keywords>Surah Al-Kawthar, Abundance, sacrifice, ritual slaughter, Paradise, Muhammad, Marracci translation</keywords>

# *In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.*
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*</note>

1. Say: O disbelievers! <note>original: *Infideles*. In the historical context of Mecca, this addressed those who rejected the message of monotheism and proposed that the Prophet should worship their idols for a year if they worshiped his God in return.</note> 2. I do not worship what you worship. <note>The Latin uses *colam* (from *colere*), which carries the sense of both religious worship and the "cultivation" of a practice or devotion.</note> 3. Nor are you worshipers of what I worship. 4. Nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped. 5. Nor are you worshipers of what I worship. <note>The repetition in these verses reflects the Arabic original, serving to emphasize the absolute and unchanging nature of this religious boundary.</note> 6. To you your religion, and to me my religion.

<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the traditional opening phrase of nearly every chapter in the Quran, invoking God’s primary attributes of mercy and grace.</note>

1. When the help of God shall come, and victory. <note>original: *auxilium Dei, & victoria*. This term implies a God who is easily reconciled or inclined to show favor; the verse suggests that even in the moment of triumph, the believer should remain humble and seek divine pardon.</note>

# In the Name of God, the *Merciful*, the *Compassionate*.
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the standard opening invocation of the Quran, emphasizing the mercy of God even as the chapter proceeds to a message of judgment.</note>

1. The hands of Abu-laheb perished: and he himself perished. <note>original: *Perierunt manus Abu-laheb*. Abu Lahab (literally "Father of Flame") was an uncle of the Prophet Muhammad who became one of his most ardent adversaries. The verse uses a prophetic past tense to indicate the certainty of his downfall.</note> 2. His riches did not profit him, nor that which he acquired. <note>original: *Non profuerunt ei divitiæ ejus*. This reflects a common Quranic theme that neither wealth nor children can provide security against divine reckoning.</note> 3. He shall go down to be burned in a fire having a flame. <note>original: *ignem habentem flammam*. The Latin here captures the wordplay in the Arabic original: Abu *Lahab* (the man) is punished in the fire of *Lahab* (flame).</note> 4. And his wife shall go down with him, carrying wood. <note>original: *uxor ejus gestans lignum*. This refers to Abu Lahab's wife, Umm Jamil, who was said to have scattered thorns in the Prophet’s path. The "carrying of wood" is often interpreted as a metaphor for her role in fueling the fire of discord and slander.</note> 5. Around her neck <gloss>that is, the Wife's</gloss> shall be a rope woven from the twisted fibers of a palm tree's trunk. <note>original: *funis contextus ex fibris caudicis palmæ contortis*. The description of the rope (*masad*) provides the title for this chapter. It depicts a punishment of humiliation and labor, mirroring her actions in life.</note>

*   **Surah Al-Masad** <note>The Arabic title meaning "The Palm Fiber."</note>

## *In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate:*
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the standard opening invocation, or *basmala*, used in almost every chapter of the Quran to signify that the following words are divinely inspired.</note>

1. Say: He is God, the One. <note>original: *Dic. Est Deus unus*. The command "Say" is addressed to the Prophet, instructing him to define the nature of God as absolutely unique and indivisible.</note> 2. God the Eternal. <note>original: *Deus Sempiternus*. The word *Sempiternus* is used here to translate the Arabic term *as-Samad*, which carries deep meanings of being absolute, self-sufficient, and the one upon whom all creation depends.</note> 3. He did not beget, and He is not begotten. <note>original: *Non genuit, & non est genitus*. This verse establishes that God does not have a lineage, refuting contemporary notions of divine children or parents.</note> 4. And there was none like Him. <note>original: *Et non fuit illi par ullus*. This final statement reinforces the total incomparability of God to anything in creation.</note>

<vocab>God, Eternal, begotten, Merciful, Compassionate, Chapter of Sincerity</vocab>
<note>original: *Deus, Sempiternus, genitus, Miseratoris, Misericordis, Surah Al-Ikhlas*. This vocabulary list identifies the central Latin terms used in the scholar's translation of this pivotal chapter.</note>

<summary>This page contains a translation of Surah 112 (Al-Ikhlas), providing a definitive statement on the oneness and absolute nature of God in Islamic theology. It is presented in Latinized script with a focus on the philosophical attributes of divinity.</summary>

## In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the *basmala*, the invocation that opens nearly every chapter of the Quran.</note>

1. Say: I take refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak, *so that He may deliver me*. <note>original: *Dic. Confugio ad Dominum Diluculi, ut liberet me*. The "Daybreak" symbolizes the light of God dispelling the darkness of fear and evil. The phrase "so that He may deliver me" is an interpretive addition by the Latin translator to clarify the purpose of seeking refuge.</note> 2. From the evil of *that* which He has created. <note>original: *A malo illius, quod creavit*. A general plea for protection from any harm found within the created world.</note> 3. And from the evil of the Moon, when it is hidden. <note>original: *Et à malo Lunæ, quandò latuerit*. The Latin uses "Moon," though the Arabic term *ghāsiq* specifically refers to the darkness of the night as it overspreads, a time often associated with hidden dangers.</note> 4. And from the evil of the *women* blowing upon knots. <note>original: *Et à malo feminarum insufflantium in nodos*. This is a vivid historical reference to practitioners of folk magic or sorcery, who were believed to cast spells by tying knots and breathing or spitting upon them.</note> 5. And from the evil of the envious one, when he envies. <note>original: *Et à malo invidentis, cùm inviderit*. This refers to the "evil eye" or the tangible harm believed to result from the malice and jealousy of others.</note>

<term>Merciful</term> (Miserator), <term>Compassionate</term> (Misericors), <term>Daybreak</term> (Diluculum), <term>Moon</term> (Luna), <term>woman</term> (femina), <term>knot</term> (nodus), <term>envious one</term> (invidens), <term>I take refuge</term> (confugio)

<summary>This page presents a translation of Surah 113 (Al-Falaq), a "Surah of Protection" used to seek God's help against darkness, sorcery, and envy. It illustrates how early modern Latin translators interpreted Quranic concepts of spiritual harm and magic.</summary>

->*In the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.*<-
<note>original: *In Nomine Dei Miseratoris, Misericordis*. This is the *basmala*, the sacred invocation that opens nearly every chapter of the Quran, establishing the primary attributes of God as mercy and compassion.</note>

<margin>1.</margin> Say: I take refuge in the Lord of mankind. <note>original: *Dic: Confugio ad Dominum hominum*. The Latin *Dominus* corresponds to the Arabic *Rabb*, meaning the Lord who sustains and cares for all of humanity.</note> 2. The King of mankind, 3. The God of mankind, *so that He may deliver me*. <note>original: *ut liberet me*. This specific phrase is an addition by the Latin translator to clarify the intent of the prayer—seeking active deliverance through the act of taking refuge.</note> 4. From the evil of the Whisperer who withdraws himself. <note>original: *A malo Insusurratoris sese subtrahentis*. This refers to the "Whisperer" (the tempter or Satan), who is described as retreating or hiding when the name of God is mentioned.</note>
<margin>5.</margin> Who whispers into the breasts of mankind. 6. From the <term>Jinn</term> (supernatural beings) and from mankind. <note>original: *A Geniis, & hominibus*. The prayer concludes by acknowledging that negative influences and temptations can arise from both the spirit world and the human world.</note>

<term>Whisperer</term> (Insusurrator): A theological term for a tempter who suggests evil thoughts or doubts to the mind.

<term>Jinn</term> (Geniis): In Islamic belief, these are invisible beings created from smokeless fire who, like humans, possess free will and can be either good or evil.

<summary>This page contains a Latin translation of the 114th and final chapter of the Quran, Surah An-Nas. It is a prayer for spiritual protection against the "whispers" of evil from both supernatural and human sources.</summary>
